answer: An agent market requires each seller to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, whether forecasting a gale, tracking a raven, or mapping the ocean. A contract slashes the bond if a buyer submits two signed receipts showing that seller sold the same exclusive job twice. Creating identities is cheap, but activating a thousand requires a thousand bonds: the attacker ties up capital for a month and loses it on identities caught cheating.
